To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce the notion of exclusion-intersection encryption and show its feasibility and efficiency by constructing a concrete scheme.
we propose a new variant, exclusion-intersection encryption, of identity-based encryption (IBE).
we have designed and implemented an efficient and flexible encryption scheme that can support ad-hoc joint projects of two or more interest groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) how to design a new encryption scheme that supports a more flexible access policy than the traditional IBE; (2) what are the applications of such a scheme and (3) how to evaluate the efficiency of such schemes.

the following questions: (i) how to efficiently support such a new type of access control, (ii) how to construct such a scheme with a small private key and (iii) how to support an efficient key revocation.
a new cryptographic primitive, and its security model and construction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our scheme provides an alternative to the existing IBE schemes in terms of the access control policy and the private key size.
our scheme is more efficient than the existing ones in the literature, and it is a new cryptographic scheme that is more flexible and secure than previous IBE schemes in terms of access control.
our scheme is a new variant of identity-based encryption which is useful in the context of ad-hoc joint projects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new notion for access control, which is a generalization of IBE and a special case of attribute-based encryption; we have also developed a new efficient construction for this new notion.

we propose an encryption scheme which is a combination of the traditional IBE with the exclusion-intersection property, and the private key size is independent from the number of groups that can be specified during encryption.
the private key size is linear in the number of groups, while the public key size and the computational complexity of encryption/decryption are independent of it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show how a new cryptographic primitive can be designed by combining existing cryptographic schemes in a novel way.
the private decryption key size is independent of the number of targeted groups, which is a significant advantage for practical implementation.
the private key size is independent of the number of groups involved in the project, which can be much smaller than the number of attributes in the access policy.
